The failing metric is line regulation (0.054 vs. 0.029 V/V), while vref, TC, power, and startup still pass. That points to a device that sets the output node's supply sensitivity without shifting the bias point much. The output PMOS M5 is the best candidate. Its drain sits at vref, so its Vds (and channel-length modulation) moves with VDD, and its current mirrors the PTAT branch. A shortened or undersized M5 would raise line sensitivity while leaving the nominal vref and TC nearly unchanged. M3 is the next most likely, since it sets the mirror gate and shares the same supply-sensitivity path. M4 is less likely because a ratio change would also move vref and TC, which still pass.

This is a judgment from the netlist and spec pattern, not a simulation. I haven't run a sweep, so the ranking is my best estimate.

The shorter effective length increases channel-length modulation, so the output current and vref track VDD more strongly, causing the line-regulation failure (0.0537 vs 0.029 V/V). Restoring M5 to match M3's sizing should bring line regulation back within spec."}
